chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:
“A woman does not undo her hair when she performs ghusl from janabah.”

Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: whoever has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating, knowing her condition, has sinned. We have already mentioned what has been transmitted regarding the prohibition of intercourse with a menstruating woman, and whoever commits something prohibited has sinned, without disagreement. Then he said: he must offer expiation—if his intercourse was at the beginning of the menstruation, then one dinar, whose value is ten dirhams of silver; if it was in the middle, then he expiates with half a dinar; and if it was at the end, then he expiates with a quarter dinar. Thus, it indicates this.

key_terms.أَثِمَ: incurred sin by committing a forbidden act
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.حَائِضٌ: a woman in the state of menstruation
key_terms.دَرَاهِمَ: silver dirhams mentioned as the dinar’s value
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: a gold coin used here as the measure of expiation
key_terms.يُكَفِّرَ: to pay expiation for the violation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on intercourse during menstruation, and must a woman undo her hair for ghusl from janabah?
ai.summary: This report states that a woman does not need to undo her hair when performing ghusl from janabah. It also sets out the ruling that intercourse with a menstruating wife, when done knowingly, is sinful and requires graded expiation depending on whether it occurred at the beginning, middle, or end of the menstrual period.
